functional_requirements.title: Digital claim submission
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall allow an employee to submit an expense claim digitally, without paper or email.
functional_requirements.reasoning: Directly restates the value proposition's 'digital submission' capability.

functional_requirements.title: Single approver dashboard
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall present every pending claim awaiting an approver's decision in one dashboard view.
functional_requirements.reasoning: Restates Phase 1's 'single approver dashboard' roadmap item as a testable capability.

functional_requirements.title: Submission-to-payment time reporting
functional_requirements.statement: The system shall record, per claim, the elapsed time from submission to payment, and expose this for reporting against a target of under 5 business days.
functional_requirements.reasoning: Directly restates NSM-01's metric and target.

content.execution_summary:
• Produced 3 functional requirements (FR-001–FR-003).
• Key decision: no compound clauses found in this vision — compound_splits is genuinely empty, not omitted.

problem_statement.summary: Expense reimbursement is slow: multi-step manager approvals lack status visibility, and Finance manually re-keys every claim, costing hours weekly.
problem_statement.reasoning: Carried forward verbatim from idea_brief_items — no drift.

target_users.summary: Employees submitting claims, approving managers, and Finance Operations staff who re-key claims and chase approvers.
target_users.reasoning: Condensed from idea_brief_items.target_users (TU-01, TU-02, TU-03) without dropping any of the three.

value_proposition.summary: Internal tool for digital claim submission, single-dashboard approver review, and clean Finance export -- removes re-keying and status-chasing.
value_proposition.reasoning: Carried forward verbatim from idea_brief_items — no drift.

market_context.summary: Alternatives: a heavier SaaS leader (Expensify) or the status quo -- neither pairs a light footprint with eliminating re-keying, the gap targeted.
market_context.reasoning: Condenses market_analysis_items' SWOT into the single most decision-relevant insight: the gap between CM-01's weakness and CM-02's weakness.

constraint_summaries.mitigation_summary: Design records so they cannot be deleted before the statutory retention period (Companies Act 2006 s.388) elapses.

north_star_metrics.target: Reduction target TBD pending stakeholder input (idea_brief_items OQ-01 unresolved)
north_star_metrics.reasoning: Carried from SM-01; no concrete target could be set since the upstream open question is still unresolved.

north_star_metrics.metric: Finance hours spent per week on claim re-keying and approver chasing
north_star_metrics.target: Reduction target TBD pending stakeholder input (idea_brief_items OQ-01 unresolved)
north_star_metrics.reasoning: Carried from SM-02; same unresolved-target limitation.

roadmap.title: Design retention-compliant record model
roadmap.description_summary: Build the claim/approval data model so records cannot be deleted before the statutory retention period — resolves OR-01 before any other feature work.

roadmap.title: Build core submission and approval dashboard
roadmap.description_summary: Digital claim submission, single approver dashboard, status visibility for employees.

roadmap.title: Finance export and pilot rollout
roadmap.description_summary: Clean export to the accounting system; pilot with one team before org-wide rollout.

open_risks.description_summary: Financial record retention (CON-02) is Amber and must be designed in from the start -- retrofitting enforcement later is harder.
No internal precedent for building approval-workflow software in-house (WK-01) -- first delivery may be slower than experienced teams.

executive_summary.summary: Replaces slow, re-keyed expense approval with digital submission, one dashboard, and clean Finance export; Amber retention risk mitigated in phase 1.
executive_summary.reasoning: Every sentence condenses a claim already present in problem_statement, market_context, regulatory_posture, or open_risks — no new claim introduced.
